source.name: Most frequent words: Polish (wordfreq, English Wiktionary)
source.notes:
The 6,000 most frequent Polish words, in frequency order.
Frequency: wordfreq 3.1 "large" list (rspeer/wordfreq; data CC BY-SA 4.0), which combines six sources: Wikipedia, OpenSubtitles, news, web text, Twitter and Reddit.
Lemmatization: PoliMorf/SGJP morphological dictionary (BSD-2-Clause), as packaged in explosion/spacy-lookups-data, plus Wiktionary headwords
Disambiguation: UD Polish PDB treebank (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), used only to split ambiguous forms such as nie (particle or pronoun); none of its text is included
Definitions and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the Wiktextract/Kaikki.org extraction in Vuizur/Wiktionary-Dictionaries (2022–23 snapshot; CC BY-SA 4.0 and GFDL)
Declension tables: PoliMorf 2.1 in the Morfologik Polish dictionary (morfologik/morfologik-stemming, BSD-2-Clause), read by our own decoder; spelling variants under 1% of the main form's frequency are left out.
Example sentences: Tatoeba (CC-BY-2.0-FR); UD Polish LFG (GPL-3.0); UD Polish PDB (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, non-commercial use only); UD Polish PUD (CC-BY-SA-4.0); AI-written (Claude) (AI-generated, not checked by a native speaker); the source of every sentence is listed in pl-sentence-credits.tsv.
See docs/VOCABULARY_SOURCES.md for licences and attribution.
